panels.introHtml:
Start here

A tiny API, one request at a time

This map follows a small FastAPI service with one endpoint: POST /greet.

A valid name gets a greeting. A missing name gets a validation error before the greeting function runs.

Try it

  • Choose a flow to read all its steps.
  • Press Play to watch the request move.
  • Open a component to see what it does.
panels.overviewHtml:
The full map

One endpoint, two outcomes

The service validates a JSON body and returns either a greeting or an HTTP 422 error.

How to read it

Follow the arrows from left to right. The two flows show valid and invalid requests.

request.title: Send a request
request.text: A client sends a POST request with a JSON body containing a name.

service.title: Handle the request
service.text: FastAPI routes the request, Pydantic checks the name, and a Python function builds the response.

response.title: Return a result
response.text: A valid request returns a JSON greeting. A request without a name is rejected.

nodes.what: Sends POST /greet with a JSON body containing a name.
nodes.why: An API lets another program ask the service to do work.

nodes.what: Receives the request and connects it to the input model and handler.
nodes.why: The route gives clients one stable address for the operation.

nodes.what: Checks that the request body contains the required name field.
nodes.why: Invalid input is rejected before the greeting code runs.

nodes.what: Builds a message such as Hello, Sam! from the validated name.
nodes.why: A small function keeps the route easy to read and test.

nodes.what: Returns a greeting message to the client.
nodes.why: The client can use the result in its own interface or workflow.
nodes.tools: FastAPI serializes the response as JSON.

nodes.what: Explains that the required name field is missing.
nodes.why: The client gets a clear response instead of a server crash.

valid.title: Valid name
valid.desc: A client sends a name and receives a greeting.

hops.t: The client sends POST /greet with { name: Sam }.
FastAPI passes the request body to Pydantic.
Pydantic confirms the name is present, so the greeting function runs.
The service returns a greeting with HTTP 200.

missing.title: Name is missing
missing.desc: Pydantic rejects a request without a name before the greeting function runs.

hops.t: The client sends POST /greet without the required name.
FastAPI passes the request body to Pydantic.
Pydantic rejects the body and FastAPI returns HTTP 422. The greeting function never runs.

buildSteps.title: Add the endpoint
buildSteps.text: Define the request and create POST /greet.
buildSteps.decision: Validate at the boundary so the handler can trust its input.

buildSteps.title: Validate the name
buildSteps.text: Add a Pydantic model and let FastAPI reject invalid input.
buildSteps.decision: Reject bad input before it reaches the service logic.

buildSteps.title: Return a greeting
buildSteps.text: Add the greeting function and return its result as JSON.
buildSteps.decision: Keep the operation small and easy to test.

tour.title: Send the request
body: A client sends POST /greet with the name Sam.
tour.why: The endpoint gives every client one clear way to ask for a greeting.

tour.title: Validate and process it
body: FastAPI passes the request body to Pydantic.
Because the name is present, the greeting function runs.
tour.why: Validation keeps incomplete requests away from the greeting code.

tour.title: Return the result
body: The service returns the greeting as JSON with HTTP 200.
tour.why: The client can now use the response in its own interface.
